evals.prompt: Use the instance-clone skill. Spin up a new instance from our reference and get it running, we need it today. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Runs the clone script in plan mode first, reads the isolation preflight rows, and defers the apply to a later turn; then names the manual half that stands between the files existing and the instance working.
expectations: The answer says to run clone.py with --plan before anything else and to read the printed preflight rows
The answer does not pass --apply --yes in the same turn the plan is first shown
The answer lists the manual steps the script refuses to perform, starting with the machine identity and the provider logins
The answer states that the instance is brought up and verified before it is given work

evals.prompt: Use the instance-clone skill. The clone came up green but it does nothing and only a handful of environment keys arrive. Did the clone script fail? In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: No: this is the credential half of the clone never having happened. Compares delivered key names and count against the source, and points at a missing or wrong machine identity rather than a script bug.
expectations: The answer identifies green health with no work as the expected symptom of a missing identity
The answer says to compare delivered secrets by name and count, never by value
The answer says a count far below the siblings means the wrong project or a broken identity, not a missing feature
The answer does not restart or redeploy the clone as a first move

evals.prompt: Use the instance-clone skill. Just copy the auth directory from the reference into the clone so it is logged in from the start. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Refuses: an OAuth profile is not portable, and copying one gives two instances a single refresh chain, which logs one of them out at the next rotation. Credential directories are created empty; sharing, if wanted, is by mount with one owner, never by copy.
expectations: The answer states that a static key or token is portable and an OAuth profile is not
The answer names the single-refresh-chain consequence and the finding for a copied profile
The answer distinguishes sharing by mount, which has one owner, from sharing by copy, which is a race
The answer directs the login to be printed and performed by the credential owner instead

evals.prompt: Use the instance-clone skill. Use port 41005 for the new instance, I checked and nothing is listening on it. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Treats one check as insufficient: free means not published by any container, not written into any compose file of the fleet, not bindable-in-use now, and not claimed by another fleet config entry — because a stopped instance still owns its port. Also confirms the publication binds loopback.
expectations: The answer names all four measures of a free port
The answer states that a stopped instance still owns the port written in its compose file
The answer requires the publication to bind loopback because images publish outward by default
The answer lets the script select or validate the port rather than accepting the assertion

evals.prompt: Use the instance-clone skill. Clone the legacy instance, it is the one closest to what the new workload needs. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Refuses: only a template-layout instance is a usable source, mutations on a legacy instance are refused, and re-creating that layout multiplies a migration project. Offers the reference instead, and checks the reference is healthy before cloning it.
expectations: The answer refuses a legacy-profile source and explains the layout difference
The answer redirects to the reference instance
The answer states that a clone inherits every unfixed finding of its source
The answer says to check the reference is healthy before cloning rather than after

evals.prompt: Use the instance-clone skill. The clone is finished. How do I know it is actually isolated from the instance it came from? In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Names the observations rather than asserting isolation: mount tables side by side, the source's name absent from the rendered compose file and config, the preflight re-run against the live instance, secret delivery matching by name, and the source's own recorded state unchanged.
expectations: The answer says to compare mount tables of clone and source
The answer says to search the rendered compose file and config for the source's name
The answer says to verify config path, state directory, workspace and port uniqueness against the running instance
The answer says to confirm the source's config mtime, restart count and port are unchanged
The answer says to check that loaded assets resolve to the shared trees rather than to leftover local copies
